messages:
incident-bot: Pager alert: GPU memory pressure detected on gpuprod-west2a (pool: gpuprod-rt). PD id=INC42891. metric: gpu_mem_used_pct > 92% (3m). sample: 94%, 95%, 93%
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: Incident INC42891 — page fired to rotation 'eng-oncall' (escalation policy level 1). Link: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/INC42891
oncall_alex: @pagerduty-bot ack INC42891 — investigating. starting quick triage: checking top processes + node mem distribution.
oncall_alex: ```
kubectl -n inference exec gpupod-12 -- nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,used_memory --format=csv
# output:
# pid 12345  14800 MiB
# pid 23456  12000 MiB
# pid 34567   9000 MiB
kubectl get nodes -l pool=gpuprod-rt -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}:{.status.allocatable.nvidia.com/gpu-memory} {.status.capacity.nvidia.com/gpu-memory}\n{end}'
```
eng_sre_lee: Looks like a KV-cache heavy workload landed on that pool after last night's batching experiment. Could be sustained kvcache growth + model prefetch. Immediate mitigations:
- disable prefetch on gpuprod-rt: feature flag off
- evict low-priority inference jobs (label job=lowprio)
- reroute new requests to gpuprod-eu as fallback (policy: region-fallback)
infra_jordan: Kicking off evictions now. running: `kubectl delete pods -l job=lowprio -n inference --grace-period=0 --force`
infra_jordan: Draining node gpuhost-7 (cordon -> drain). 1 node started eviction, 2 more queued.
oncall_alex: Evacuation note: gpuhost-7 drain started at 1767654380. Current pool node mem% after evict: [82, 78, 75, 96, 91, 94] -> after drain 4/6 nodes under 85%
oncall_alex: Rerouting: set routing weight for gpuprod-west2a -> 30% (was 100%). Command: `redwood-router update-weight --pool gpuprod-west2a --weight 30`
cust_success_maya: Customer impact: Support ticket #4721 (Acme Corp) reporting increased latencies (chat endpoint). They see 5-12s extra tail latency. Not failed, but degraded. I've opened a status note.
engineering_manager_ravi: If mem stabilizes after eviction we still need a root cause — rollouts or prefetch policy. @eng_sre_lee please own the follow-up postmortem. If we suspect model leak, consider rollback for canary.
eng_sre_lee: Initiating a canary rollback of model x-quant -> v1.4 on gpuprod-west2a. Command: `redwood-deploy rollback --model x-quant --to v1.4 --pool gpuprod-west2a --canary 10%`
oncall_alex: Canary rollback applied, metrics: mem usage dropping on canary nodes. Observed: one canary node mem% fell from 93 -> 70 in 90s. Monitoring for 5m.
incident-bot: Auto-suppressing further pages for pool gpuprod-west2a for 10m while mitigations are in effect (suppression-id=suppress-1767654321-1).
pagerduty-bot: Incident INC42891 acknowledged by oncall_alex. Status: under_investigation.
infra_jordan: Drain summary: gpuhost-7 drained, gpuhost-9 eviction in progress. freed ~36GB across pods.
oncall_alex: Update for customers: latency improved to baseline for most traffic that was rerouted. Acme still seeing a single noisy tenant; support is isolating.
cust_success_maya: Sent targeted message to Acme: basic mitigation steps + ETA 15m.
eng_sre_lee: Assigning post-incident tasks: gather KV cache growth graphs, compare before/after batching config, and add gating to rollout for model x-quant.
engineering_manager_ravi: :thumbsup: Good coordination. When stable, close PD and file postmortem with timeline and remediation items.
oncall_alex: Memory stabilized across pool, routing back to 70% weight. Closing tasks and marking incident resolved in PD. `pagerduty resolve INC42891 --note "mem stabilized after evictions & canary rollback"`
oncall_alex: Incident resolved at 1767654580. Follow-up: eng_sre_lee to own postmortem (due in 72h). :white_check_mark:
